questions.q: What is the heir of a Scottish baron styled?
questions.why: A survey of Scots law of 1936 puts the two in one sentence: the heir of a peer is “Master”, the heir of a baron is “younger of”.

questions.q: How did the style “Much Honoured” begin?
options: As a grant from the Crown
questions.why: “Much honoured” began as a courtesy of address, not as the mark of a rank.

questions.q: The old Scots Act on robes gave the barons and the lords of parliament a mantle of which colour?
questions.why: The Act of 1455 gave the lords of parliament one red mantle, which Lord Lyon Innes of Learney read as the barons’, great and small.

questions.q: What did the Treaty of Union do with the baron’s court?
options: Joined it to the English courts
questions.why: This is the Article that touched the baron: his court was a heritable jurisdiction, and the Treaty preserved it as property.

questions.q: Of old, a baron on trial for a crime had the right to be tried by whom?
questions.why: The old law says it in terms: “ane Earle, be Earles; ane Baron, be Barons”.
